html:
The Ngandi were an Aboriginal Australian people of southern Arnhem Land in the Northern Territory, in the country drained by rivers flowing to the Roper and the Gulf. They are not the same as the Ngandji, another people of the region. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their language is not part of the Pama-Nyungan family that covers most of Australia, but one of the many separate families of the far north. Little is recorded of their early history. Neighbours on the map include the Ngalkbun, the Nunggubuyu, the Rembarnga and the Yolngu. The Roper River mission, opened in 1908, drew many people of the area. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
